htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. Help improve this component To help make sure that this page is useful, relevant and up to date, you can: take part in the ‘Textarea’ discussion on GitHub and share your research propose a change on GitHub – read more about how to propose changes in GitHub Need help? If you’ve got a question about the GOV.UK Design System, contact the team. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. Help improve this component To help make sure that this page is useful, relevant and up to date, you can: take part in the ‘Textarea’ discussion on GitHub and share your research propose a change on GitHub – read more about how to propose changes in GitHub Need help? They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. Help improve this component To help make sure that this page is useful, relevant and up to date, you can: take part in the ‘Textarea’ discussion on GitHub and share your research propose a change on GitHub – read more about how to propose changes in GitHub Need help? If you’ve got a question about the GOV.UK Design System, contact the team. htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. Help improve this component To help make sure that this page is useful, relevant and up to date, you can: take part in the ‘Textarea’ discussion on GitHub and share your research propose a change on GitHub – read more about how to propose changes in GitHub Need help? htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. Help improve this component To help make sure that this page is useful, relevant and up to date, you can: take part in the ‘Textarea’ discussion on GitHub and share your research propose a change on GitHub – read more about how to propose changes in GitHub Need help? If you’ve got a question about the GOV.UK Design System, contact the team. htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. Help improve this component To help make sure that this page is useful, relevant and up to date, you can: take part in the ‘Textarea’ discussion on GitHub and share your research propose a change on GitHub – read more about how to propose changes in GitHub Need help? If you’ve got a question about the GOV.UK Design System, contact the team. Nunjucks macro options

Use options to customise the appearance, content and behaviour of a component when using a macro, for example, changing the text.

Some options are required for the macro to work; these are marked as “Required” in the option description. Deprecated options are marked as “Deprecated”.

If you’re using Nunjucks macros in production with “html” options, or ones ending with “html”, you must sanitise the HTML to protect against cross-site scripting exploits.

Nunjucks macro options

Use options to customise the appearance, content and behaviour of a component when using a macro, for example, changing the text.

Some options are required for the macro to work; these are marked as “Required” in the option description. Deprecated options are marked as “Deprecated”.

If you’re using Nunjucks macros in production with “html” options, or ones ending with “html”, you must sanitise the HTML to protect against cross-site scripting exploits.

htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. Help improve this component To help make sure that this page is useful, relevant and up to date, you can: take part in the ‘Textarea’ discussion on GitHub and share your research propose a change on GitHub – read more about how to propose changes in GitHub Need help? If you’ve got a question about the GOV.UK Design System, contact the team. htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. Help improve this component To help make sure that this page is useful, relevant and up to date, you can: take part in the ‘Textarea’ discussion on GitHub and share your research propose a change on GitHub – read more about how to propose changes in GitHub Need help? If you’ve got a question about the GOV.UK Design System, contact the team. htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. Help improve this component To help make sure that this page is useful, relevant and up to date, you can: take part in the ‘Textarea’ discussion on GitHub and share your research propose a change on GitHub – read more about how to propose changes in GitHub Need help? htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. Help improve this component To help make sure that this page is useful, relevant and up to date, you can: take part in the ‘Textarea’ discussion on GitHub and share your research propose a change on GitHub – read more about how to propose changes in GitHub Need help? If you’ve got a question about the GOV.UK Design System, contact the team. htmlAfterStep.bodyTextExcerpt: SR Output Tool VoiceOver scan start marker Skip to main content Design System Search Design system Get started Styles Components Patterns Community Accessibility Pages in this section Accordion Back link Breadcrumbs Button Character count Checkboxes Cookie banner Date input Details Error message Error summary Exit this page Fieldset File upload Generic header GOV.UK footer GOV.UK header Inset text Notification banner Pagination Panel Password input Phase banner Radios Select Service navigation Skip link Summary list Table Tabs Tag Task list Text input Textarea Warning text Home Components Textarea Open this example in a new tab : textarea HTML Nunjucks When to use this component Use the textarea component when you need to let users enter an amount of text that’s longer than a single line. When not to use this component Users can find open-ended questions difficult to answer. It might be better to break up one complex question into a series of simple ones, for example where users can select from options using a Radios component. If you need to ask an open question Do not use the textarea component if you need to let users enter shorter answers no longer than a single line, such as a phone number or name. In this case, you should use the Text input component. How it works You must label textareas. Placeholder text is not a suitable substitute for a label, as it disappears when users click inside the textarea. Labels must be aligned above the textarea they refer to. They should be short, direct and written in sentence case. Do not use colons at the end of labels. There are 2 ways to use the textarea component. You can use HTML or, if you’re using Nunjucks or the GOV.UK Prototype Kit, you can use the Nunjucks macro. Open this example in a new tab : textarea second HTML Nunjucks Use appropriately-sized textareas Make the height of a textarea proportional to the amount of text you expect users to enter. You can set the height of a textarea by specifying the rows attribute. Open this example in a new tab : textarea appropriately-sized with rows – textarea HTML Nunjucks Do not disable copy and paste Users will often need to copy and paste information into a textarea, so do not stop them from doing this. If you’re asking more than one question on the page If you’re asking more than one question on the page, do not set the contents of the <label> as the page heading. Read more about asking multiple questions on Question pages. Open this example in a new tab : textarea without a heading – textarea HTML Nunjucks Limiting the number of characters If there’s a good reason to limit the number of characters users can enter, you can use the Character count component. Error messages Error messages should be styled like this: Open this example in a new tab : textarea with error – textarea HTML Nunjucks Make sure errors follow the guidance in the Error message component and have specific error messages for specific error states. If the input is empty Say ‘Enter [whatever it is]’. For example, ‘Enter summary’. If the input is too long Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or less’. For example, ‘Summary must be 400 characters or less’. If the input is too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be [number] characters or more’. For example, ‘Summary must be 10 characters or more’. If the input is too long or too short Say ‘[whatever it is] must be between [number] and [number] characters’. For example, ‘Summary must be between 10 and 400 characters’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must not include [characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must not include è and £’. If the input uses characters that are not allowed and you do not know what the characters are Say ‘[whatever it is] must only include [list of allowed characters]’. For example, ‘Summary must only include letters a to z, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes. Help improve this component To help make sure that this page is useful, relevant and up to date, you can: take part in the ‘Textarea’ discussion on GitHub and share your research propose a change on GitHub – read more about how to propose changes in GitHub Need help? If you’ve got a question about the GOV.UK Design System, contact the team. Nunjucks macro options

Use options to customise the appearance, content and behaviour of a component when using a macro, for example, changing the text.

Some options are required for the macro to work; these are marked as “Required” in the option description. Deprecated options are marked as “Deprecated”.

If you’re using Nunjucks macros in production with “html” options, or ones ending with “html”, you must sanitise the HTML to protect against cross-site scripting exploits.
